app.title: Hydro Lens — calibrated optical screening of microscope images for microplastic particles
app.summary: The person first sets the optical scale on a calibration page. They can compute microns per pixel from a stage micrometer image or enter a measured line distance by hand, then check the scale against reference beads and save it with an expiry date. On the analysis page they upload a microscope image or pick a demo reference, then run a pipeline that preprocesses the image, detects candidate particles, sizes them and scores confidence. The results show headline numbers, active flags, the annotated image next to the preprocessed one, a size histogram and a table with one row per particle. The person then enters the filtered volume and dilution to get particles per litre and downloads a JSON report. Sizes and concentration are blocked until a valid calibration exists.

task.text: Count, classify and size candidate particles in a calibrated microscope image, estimate their concentration in the sampled water, and flag samples that need lab confirmation.

data.text: Microscope images of filtered samples, each turned into a table of detected objects with a class, a confidence score and physical sizes, plus a saved calibration record that converts pixels to microns.
data.item: a candidate particle detected in one microscope image of a filter

stage.text: screening calibrated microscope images of filtered samples to get counts, sizes and concentration, before lab confirmation

mechanism.text: A sidebar radio switches between the analysis page and a calibration wizard, and shows the calibration status on every page. That status unlocks or blocks the quantitative tabs. After a run, a row of metric cards and a flags expander sit above tabs: two images side by side, a size histogram, a sortable particle table, a concentration form and a JSON export.

field.text: calibrated particle detection and sizing in optical microscopy for water-quality screening

workflow.name: count and size objects in an image against a calibrated scale, then estimate their concentration

steps.step: set and validate the measurement scale before measuring
steps.here: Microns per pixel are computed by FFT from a stage micrometer image, or from a measured pixel distance and a number of divisions. The scale is checked against 10, 50 and 100 µm reference beads and saved with magnification, camera and an expiry date.
Upload a JPG, PNG or TIFF microscope image, or pick a demo reference (mixed sample, blank filter control or stage micrometer). A banner shows whether calibration is active, stale or missing.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: 'Run Screening Pipeline' applies median blur and CLAHE, runs YOLO detection, measures Feret diameters and ECD with OpenCV, and scores confidence. Particle count, sample confidence, the lab-confirmation flag, imaged area and inference time appear as cards, with the active flags listed below them.
The annotated image, with boxes coloured by confidence tier, sits next to the preprocessed input.
A bar chart counts particles in equivalent-circular-diameter bins, and a table lists each particle's class, confidence, Feret max and min, ECD, aspect ratio and lab-flag reasons.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Enter the filtered water volume in mL and a dilution factor to get the estimated particles per litre from the count and the imaged area.
The full report is shown as JSON and can be downloaded as a file named by sample ID.

distinctive: A calibration gate controls the output: without a valid, unexpired scale factor, sizes, the size histogram and concentration are blocked, and only the count is reported.
Calibration expires after a set number of days. A stale calibration halves the quality factor in the sample confidence score.

Sample confidence is mean detection confidence × calibration quality × coverage factor. A rule set sends the sample to lab confirmation on low confidence, large size, high aspect ratio or a poorly supported class.
Scale validation compares measured reference beads against their nominal sizes, with a percentage error for each bead.
Concentration is extrapolated from one field of view to the whole sample, using the filtered volume and the dilution factor.

parts.title: Calibration status and wizard
parts.summary: Shows the active scale factor and its validity in the sidebar, and walks the person through computing, validating and saving a new microns-per-pixel calibration.

parts.title: Sample analysis
parts.summary: Shows the calibration banner, takes an uploaded or demo microscope image, and runs the detection, sizing and confidence pipeline.

parts.title: Metric cards and screening flags
parts.summary: Shows the particle count, sample confidence, the lab-confirmation flag, imaged area and inference time, followed by the list of active screening flags.

parts.title: Annotated and preprocessed images
parts.summary: Places the image with confidence-coloured detection boxes next to the contrast-enhanced input.

parts.title: Size distribution
parts.summary: Counts particles in equivalent-circular-diameter bins and draws them as a bar chart, or shows a blocking notice when calibration is missing.
